headline: Approved moving $59,375 to cover expenses and a $50,000 contingency transfer for motor vehicle service repairs.
summary: Commissioners heard public comments on Ridge Road traffic and speeding and on LPR cameras. They approved two Board of Finance requests, one moving $59,375 for expenses and one transferring $50,000 from contingency for vehicle repairs. They also received an update on the ATED program and a joint Police and Fire Training Facility at 30 Cross Street.
decisions: Approved the minutes of the September 18, 2026 regular meeting, unanimously.
Approved the monthly reports and placed them on file, unanimously.
Approved the appropriation request to move $59,375 to cover expenses, unanimously.
Approved the transfer of $50,000 from contingency to cover motor vehicle service repairs, unanimously.
Placed the K-9 calendar fundraiser on file, unanimously.

decision_titles: $50,000 contingency transfer for motor vehicle service repairs
plain_text:
BOARD OF POLICE COMMISSIONERS 
REGULAR MEETING 
                                                      OCTOBER 20, 2026, AT 6:00 p.m. 
COUNCIL CHAMBERS 
 
 
PRESENT:             ABSENT:  
Mayor Ellen Zoppo-Sassu, Chairperson   Commissioner Terry Lewis           
Commissioner Rory Ghio – via Zoom 
Commissioner Dean Kilbourne         
Commissioner Paul Lemieux 
Commissioner Gloria Sapp Smith 
Council Member Sue Tyler               
Board of Finance Liaison, Jon Mace 
 
 
 
1. CALL TO ORDER 
Mayor Zoppo-Sassu called the meeting to order at 6:00 P.M. 
 
2. PRESENTATION OF AWARDS 
None 
  
3. PUBLIC PARTICIPATION 
Mae Palmisano, 83 Aldbourne Drive, thanked Officer Trey Frechette for helping with an unwanted 
person on her Queen Street property. 
 
Nick Palmer, 69 Cronin Street, expressed his opposition to the LPR cameras. 
 
Amy Tasino, 50 Ridge Road, asked the Police Department for help with traffic and speeding on Ridge 
Road. 
 
Joe Keleita, 227 Ashley Road, said his daughter lives on Ridge Road and asked the Police Department 
for assistance with traffic and speeding on Ridge Road. 
 
Robert Cochran, 32 Ridge Road, again asked the Police Department for assistance with traffic and 
speeding on Ridge Road. 
 
4. APPROVAL OF MINUTES 
Council Member Tyler moved to APPROVE THE MINUTES FROM THE SEPTEMBER 18, 2026 
REGULAR POLICE BOARD MEETING, Seconded by Commissioner Sapp Smith. 
 
VOTE: UNANIMOUSLY PASSED  
 
5. APPROVAL OF VARIOUS MONTHLY REPORTS 
Commissioner Kilbourne moved to APPROVE MONTHLY REPORTS AND PLACE ON FILE, 
Seconded by Commissioner Sapp-Smith. 
 
              VOTE: UNANIMOUSLY PASSED
6. CORRESPONDENCE 
None 
 
7. COMMITTEE MINUTES 
i. Traffic Sub-Committee Meeting 
Council Member Tyler informed the Board that the Traffic Sub-Committee will adjust its schedule 
effective January 2027.  The Board will meet bimonthly, and the meeting time has changed to 5:30 p.m. 
 
8. OLD BUSINESS 
a.  Chief Morello 
i. Tuttle Road Rt. 69 Light Timing 
Chief Morello reviewed the memo attached to the packet for information purposes. 
 
8.2     Police Commissioners 
None 
 
9.  NEW BUSINESS 
9.1   Chief Morello 
i. Chief’s Report 
Chief Morello reviewed the Chief’s report. 
 
ii. Board of Finance Request 
Commissioner Kilbourne moved to APPROVE THE APPROPRIATION REQUEST TO MOVE 
$59,375 TO COVER EXPENSES, Seconded by Commissioner Sapp-Smith. 
 
              VOTE: UNANIMOUSLY PASSED 
 
iii. Board of Finance Request 
Commissioner Sapp-Smith moved to APPROVE THE TRANSFER FROM CONTINGENCY 
REQUEST OF $50,000 TO COVER MOTOR VEHICLE SERVICE REPAIRS, seconded by 
Commissioner Lemieux. 
 
              VOTE: UNANIMOUSLY PASSED 
iv. K-9 Calendar Fundraiser 
Commissioner Lemieux moved to PLACE ON FILE, Seconded by Commissioner Kilbourne. 
 
              VOTE: UNANIMOUSLY PASSED 
 
9.2 Police Commissioners 
i. ATED Update 
Mayor Zoppo-Sassu informed the Board that we are looking to execute the contract with SiteStream. At 
that point, they will begin working with the Department to compile all the data required for the State 
application process. Once they identify the intersections, they will compile the data and return it to the 
Police Commission for review, prioritization, and submission to DOT. Installation is expected in the 
spring. 
 
We have also been working on the joint Police and Fire Training Facility, which will be located at 30 
Cross Street.  We received $3.1 million from the Federal Government for this project, and we are 
working with the State; we have also bonded $2.5 million.
10. ADJOURNMENT 
Council Member Tyler moved to ADJOURN, seconded by Commissioner Sapp-Smith. 
  
             VOTE: UNANIMOUSLY PASSED 
 
 
The regular meeting of the Board of Police Commissioners called for the 20th day of October, 2026, 
was HEREBY ADJOURNED AT 6:36 p.m. 
 
 
 
                   Lisa Ziogas                   Recording Secretary
